# Temple Scroll Column 63 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 63:2 — "to the mouth of the sword" vs. "to the sword" vs. "slaughter with the sword"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "put the inhabitants of that city to the mouth of the sword" | Literal לפי חרב |
| LOGOS | "put the inhabitants of that city to the sword" | Standard English idiom |
| PNEUMA | "slaughter every inhabitant of that city with the sword" | Dynamic, visceral |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "put to the sword." Idiomatic English that retains gravitas; EMET's "mouth of the sword" is a Hebraism; PNEUMA's "slaughter" adds interpretive violence beyond the text's register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 63:3 — "before me" with or without "as a whole offering/sacrifice"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "burn with fire the city... before me" | Literal — no added gloss |
| LOGOS | "burn the city... as a whole offering before me" | Adds "whole offering" to clarify חרם theology |
| PNEUMA | "burn the entire city... as a sacrifice to me" | Interpretive — makes חרם explicit as sacrifice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's approach — "before me" without added gloss. The text says לפני, not כליל or עולה. LOGOS and PNEUMA import sacrificial language not present in this line.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 63:7 — "evil defect" vs. "defect whatever" vs. "defective in any way"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "any evil defect" | Literal כל דבר רע |
| LOGOS | "any blemish or defect whatever" | Formal, comprehensive |
| PNEUMA | "defective in any way" | Simplified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "any blemish or defect whatever." Covers the full semantic range; EMET's "evil defect" is awkward in English; PNEUMA oversimplifies the dual terminology.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 63:13 — "fear me" vs. "revere me" vs. "honor me" — ירא

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fear me" | Literal ליראה |
| LOGOS | "revere me" | Formal, captures respectful awe |
| PNEUMA | "honor me" | Accessible modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "revere me." In the tithing context, ירא connotes reverent awe rather than terror (EMET) or mere respect (PNEUMA).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 63:16 — "strong drink" vs. "beer" — שכר

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "strong drink" | Traditional rendering |
| LOGOS | "strong drink" | Standard scholarly term |
| PNEUMA | "beer" | Modern equivalent of ancient שכר |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS "strong drink." While שכר may include beer, the term covers various fermented beverages. "Beer" is too narrow and anachronistic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
